title: Operational Governance Technical Reference
readerIntent: Audit lifecycle, observability, runtime governance, and operational evidence.
owner: Runtime lifecycle, diagnostics, audit, health, and nDynamo contracts
summary: Every operational capability defines readiness, bounded lifecycle, safe signals, authority, failure, recovery, retention, and tests.

sections.heading: Lifecycle states and authority
items: nConfig owns process start, readiness transition, signal handling, drain, shutdown, and terminal state. Modules contribute bounded hooks but cannot create competing lifecycle coordinators.
Liveness states that the process exists; readiness states that composed required modules can accept work. Degraded optional control-plane integrations do not automatically block customer traffic.
Lifecycle identity names environment, server, node, process, module, provider, state, revision, timestamp, and safe reason category.

sections.heading: Startup, drain, and shutdown
items: Classify dependencies as required or optional, initialize required authority before readiness, and recover optional registration or observation asynchronously with bounded backoff.
SIGTERM and SIGINT mark readiness false, reject new work, stop claims, drain within deadline, close resources in dependency order, and preserve recoverable state.
SIGKILL and hard OOM cannot run hooks; replicas, external supervision, durable leases, idempotency, and reconciliation provide resilience.

sections.heading: Governed runtime changes
items: Only explicitly supported mutable contracts enter nDynamo governance. Static layered configuration, secrets, code, and prototype-sensitive paths remain outside runtime mutation.
Preview calculates impact without side effects; approval binds actor and immutable digest; activation validates scope and revision; audit records outcome; rollback uses the same owner.
BackOffice, CLI, MCP, and AI tools invoke governance APIs and display evidence but never write governed persistence directly.

sections.heading: Observability and incidents
items: Correlate request, job, event, workflow, publication, import, provider call, configuration activation, and target outcome using safe bounded context.
Logs explain events, metrics expose trends, traces show paths, health reports service state, and audit proves governed intent; none replaces the owning business record.
Incident flow detects, assesses customer impact, contains, preserves evidence, recovers authority, reconciles derived state, verifies outcome, and documents prevention.

sections.heading: Verification checklist
items: Test clean and partial startup, ambiguous topology, required and optional outages, rolling restart, repeated signals, stuck work, lease takeover, crash, and recovery.
Test runtime preview, stale digest, unauthorized approval, concurrent activation, forbidden path, owner failure, audit, rollback, and multi-node visibility.
Measure startup, readiness, drain, hook, backlog, lease, retry, reconciliation, and activation behavior; document alerts, runbooks, service objectives, and known limitations.

sections.heading: Checklist
items: Owned resource, contributor name/order/deadline, required/optional dependency, readiness, drain, shutdown, and cleanup.
Trace/correlation, tenant, module, operation, safe outcomes, metrics cardinality, audit, masking, retention, and alerts.
Preview, approval, actor separation, digest/revision, activation, conflict, cleanup, rollback, backup, and restore.
Positive, negative, timeout, restart, hard-failure, contract, integration, distributed topology, security, load, incident-recovery, and regression tests.
